name: htmlhint

alt-require.description: Alt of img must be present and alt of area[href] and input[type=image] must be set value.

attr-no-duplication.description: The same attribute can't be specified twice.

attr-unsafe-chars.description: Attribute value can't not use unsafe chars.

attr-value-double-quotes.description: Attribute value must closed by double quotes.

head-script-disabled.description: The script tag can not be used in head.

href-abs-or-rel.description: Href must be absolute or relative.

html-lang-require.description: The lang attribute of an <html> element must be present and should be valid.

id-class-ad-disabled.description: Id and class can not use ad keyword, it will blocked by adblock software.

id-class-value.description: Id and class value must meet some rules: underline, dash, hump.

id-unique.description: ID attributes must be unique in the document.

space-tab-mixed-disabled.description: Spaces and tabs can not mixed in front of line.

src-not-empty.description: Src of img(script,link) must set value. Empty of src will visit current page twice.

style-disabled.description: Style tag can not be used.

tag-self-close.description: The empty tag must closed by self.

schema.title: JSON schema for HTMLHint configuration files

description: Dear Development Team, Please review the updated HTML coding standards that we’ll be applying to all new pages. Every document must start with an HTML5 doctype placed at the very top, and the  element is required to carry a valid lang attribute. All tag names should be lowercase, and every tag must be properly paired; we are no longer mandating self‑closing syntax for empty elements. Within the  section a  element is compulsory, and while script tags are still permitted there, any inline scripts or inline style attributes are now forbidden. The <style> tag itself is disallowed, and all attribute values must be quoted with double quotes and cannot be empty. Attribute names are to be written in lowercase, duplicate attributes on the same element are prohibited, and we will not be checking for unsafe characters inside attribute values. All href attributes must use absolute URLs, and src attributes on <img>, <script>, and <link> elements must never be left empty. Special characters should always be escaped, and leading whitespace at the start of lines may contain spaces only—mixing tabs with spaces is not allowed. For element identification, each id must be unique across the document and must not contain the substring “ad”. Class names share the same restriction, and both IDs and classes should follow dash (hyphen‑separated) naming conventions. Finally, every <img> as well as <area href> and <input type="image"> must include a non‑empty alt attribute. Please ensure these rules are reflected in your code reviews and automated linting pipelines.
